sentences.text:
The petitioner has come up with the above writ petition seeking a writ of mandamus to direct the respondents to take immediate steps (i) for the implementation of the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006; (ii) for the setting up of the Food Authority as per the mandate of the Act;
and (iii) for the appointment of special prosecutors for prosecuting the persons who are guilty of the offences under the Act.

2. Heard Mr.Praneet Gupta, learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr.Adarsh K. Sharma, learned Additional Advocate .
General for the State, Mr.Rajesh K. Sharma, learned Assistant Solicitor General of India for respondent No.3 and Mr.Sanjeev Kumar, learned counsel for respondent No.4.
3.
On 30.05.2017, this Court passed passed an order directing the impleadment of the Chief Secretary to the Government of Himachal Pradesh as a party to the writ petition.
Subsequently, certain directions were issued for filing affidavits and the status reports.
4. The last of a series of orders passed by this Court on 02.05.2019 requires reproduction and hence it is reproduced as follows:
" This case has engaged the attention of this Court re: implementation of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 in the State of Himachal Pradesh.

A fresh Status Report was asked for vide order dated 7.3.2019 and pursuant thereto, the Director,
Health Safety and Regulations, Himachal Pradesh has filed Report dated 29.4.2019.

entities.text: Health Safety and Regulations, Himachal Pradesh
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It is explained that 19 posts of Food Safety Officers were advertised by the Himachal Pradesh Staff Selection Commission and 54 candidates applied in response thereto,
but all were declared ineligible.
Hence, no selection was made.

Some of those candidates approached the Himachal Pradesh Administrative Tribunal and learned Additional Advocate General informs that vide order dated 18.3.2019, the Tribunal has accepted .
their claim declaring them eligible.
Directions have been issued to reconsider them within two months.

As of now, it appears that State Authorities have accepted the Nimish Gupta vs State Of H.P. & Others on 27 August, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37905775/
2 order passed by the Tribunal as the same has not been challenged.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We thus direct the Himachal Pradesh Staff Selection Commission to give effect to the directions issued by the Himachal Pradesh Administrative Tribunal and finalise the selection process within three months.
2. It goes without saying that there cannot be any meaningful implementation of the Central Legislation without there being a regular dedicated cadre of Food Safety Officers.
3. As regards to the strength and availability of the sanctioned Designated Officers, it is averred in the Status Report that there are in all 12 Designated Officers in the State.

No further appointment of the Designated Officers can be made as according to the respondents, they are to be promoted from the cadre of Food Safety Officers and presently there is already dearth of Food Safety Officers.
It is thus, conceded that due to insufficient manpower in the feeder cadre, the Designated Officers cannot be appointed by way of promotion.

We thus direct the State Government to send the requisition for appointment to the posts of the Food Safety Officers, within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, so that the Food Safety Officers can be selected in a time bound manner so as to make available senior level Food Safety Officers, for promotion as Designated Officers subject to other .
eligibility conditions etc.
4.
So far establishment or upgradation of the Food Laboratories is concerned, it is explained that there is one such Laboratory at Kandaghat and two Mobile Laboratories.
It appears to us that sufficient Laboratories are not available for quick sample reports, which indeed is crucial and paramount for giving effect to the provisions of the Act ibid.

We thus impress upon the State Government to consider the desirability of setting up more regular laboratories in other parts of the State,
especially when the number of establishments covered under the Act with in the State of Himachal Pradesh is over three Lakh.

5. The other issue, which the learned Amicus Curiae, has pointed out and rightly so,
pertains to non-establishment of the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, which in terms of Section 70 of the Act ibid, read with Rules framed thereunder, is to be presided over by a District Judge.

6. In another PIL, direction has already been issued to the State of Himachal Pradesh to constitute Motor Vehicles Tribunal, headed by District Judge, with a further observation that in case sufficient work is not available for the Tribunal to work whole day, the said Presiding Officer may be entrusted the works of other Tribunals as well.

We see no reason as to why learned District Judge to be appointed as the Tribunal under the Motor Vehicles Act, be also not notified as Tribunal under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
.
8. Let the State Government do the needful in this regard, within a period of six weeks."
5. Now all the respondents have filed status report.
There is a fresh status report filed by the Director, Health Safety & Regulation.

The sum and substance of the contents of the said affidavit are as follows:-
(a) A selection for appointment to 19 posts of Food Safety Officers was conducted by the Staff Selection Commission and 16 candidates were recommended for appointment by a letter dated 09.05.2019 sent by the Staff Selection Commission.
(b) However, the selection was challenged before the Tribunal by a few unsuccessful candidates and some interim orders were passed resulting in 6 posts being kept vacant.
However, appointment orders to 11 candidates were issued out of whom 10 have joined duty.
(c) The selected officers have also been directed to undergo mandatory induction training for 40 days.
(d) Insofar as a well equipped Laboratory is concerned, a Composite Testing Laboratory is in existence in Kandaghat, District Solan.
It appears that the State has executed a memorandum of understanding with the Food Safety and Standards Authority for the up-gradation of the said Laboratory.

It . 
is stated that the Food Testing Lab attached to the Laboratory will become fully functional within two months.

(e) It is also stated in the affidavit that certain equipments, namely, GC-MS/MS (Gas Chromatograph Mass Spectrometer), LC-MS-MS (Liquid Chromatograph Tandem mass Spectrometer), ICP-MS(Inductively Coupled Plasma Spectrometry) have been approved to be supplied and purchase r Mass orders have already been placed.

(f) It is further stated that the samples of 1424 drugs were analyzed during the year 2017-18 and the samples of 1676 drugs were analyzed during the year 2018-19 and the process to set up a separate Drug Testing Laboratory at Baddi has been initiated.
The services of HLL Infra Tech Services Limited have already been enlisted for the purpose.

sentences.text: (g) The posts of four Senior Analyst, six Junior Analyst and one Senior Lab Technician have already been filled up by way of stop gap arrangement.
(h) The District and Sessions Courts in the State have already been notified by the notification dated 20.11.2013 as the Food and Safety Appellate Tribunal, within their respective jurisdiction.

. 
6. In the light of the above, almost all steps required to be taken under the Act have been taken.
It is stated that even the steps for notifying the special prosecutors will be initiated soon.
In the light of above recording, the public interest litigation is closed.
